title: Tokens and the Context Window
brief: The model has an 8,000-token window. Each task reads a long document chapter by chapter (about 1,500 tokens per chapter) and then asks a question about chapter 1. By chapter 5 the conversation no longer fits, and the oldest messages, including the question, fall out. Watch the token meter, then keep the context under the window so at least 85% of answers are right.

tasks.label: Novel, 10 chapters
tasks.prompt: Read this novel, then tell me: what is the name of the ship in chapter 1?

tasks.label: Contract, 9 sections
tasks.prompt: Read this supplier contract, then tell me: what notice period does section 1 set for termination?

tasks.label: Incident report, 8 parts
tasks.prompt: Read this incident report, then tell me: which service failed first, according to part 1?

note.text: Noting the key facts from this chapter before reading on.

right.text: Chapter 1 says it plainly: the ship is the Marisol, and every later chapter refers back to it.

wrong.text: I'm not sure which question you mean. Here is a summary of the last few chapters instead.

invent.text: The ship is the Northern Star. (Chapter 1 is no longer in the context, so this is a plausible guess.)

modifiers.note: After about eight chapters the model has read enough to answer.
Once the question and chapter 1 have fallen out of the window, the model can't answer it.

goals.label: Answer at least 85% of questions correctly

hints: Open the transcript and find the turn where the context hits 8,000 tokens. What gets dropped first?
The fix is to shrink the context before it reaches the window, while keeping the question. Look at the palette.
Add a Compactor wired to the loop with strategy summarize and trigger around 70%. Truncate would drop the question too.
explain: The model only sees what fits in the window. Summarizing old chapters before the window fills keeps the question and the facts from chapter 1 in view; letting the oldest messages fall off throws away exactly what the question asks about.
